title: Shrink lint snapshot caching, add staged presubmit hints and release sanity scorer
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Our presubmit lint stage has been a major CI time and flakiness contributor for monorepo PRs, largely due to full snapshot recalculations for every workspace change and noisy release-checklist manual reviews. This PR reorganizes the lint snapshot cache into per-package, content-hashed blobs, introduces staged presubmit hints (a small fast lane that runs language-level quickchecks), and adds a release-sanity scorer that emits a machine-readable sanity score for release automation to consume. Motivation: reduce presubmit latency for small patchsets, make longtests/lint failures easier to triage, and provide a quantifiable pre-merge signal for release automation to detect risky rollouts. Summary of changes: - Introduce pkg-lint-cache: per-package cache keyed by file set fingerprint and tool version. Cache is stored in the existing artifact store (ci-cache/) and falls back to full snapshot when missing. - Add a staged-presubmit job in workflows/ci-presubmit.yml: quick-lint (fast regex/AST smoke), unit-style checks, and a cache-warm step. This job runs in <2m for small PRs. - Add release-sanity-scorer binary (go): computes a JSONL score combining: changed files surface area, presence of security labels, modified infra manifests, and lint regression delta. Exposes SCORE env var and writes scorer.json to artifacts. - Update npm/python/go lint runners to emit minimal metadata required for the scorer and cache keys. - Tests: integration harness that simulates incremental file edits and validates cache hits/misses and scorer outputs. - Docs: doc/dev/ci-presubmit-quickstart.md and internal runbook for the scorer thresholds. Rollout plan: 1) Merge feature behind feature flag CI_LINT_FASTPATH=true. 2) Opt-in select teams for 1 week. 3) Gradual default-on after 2 weeks of telemetry. Backout: revert the feature flag and the workflow change; cache format is versioned so old artifacts are ignored. Checklist: - [x] per-package cache hashing and store - [x] staged-presubmit workflow added with fast-lint path - [x] release-sanity-scorer implemented and integrated into artifacts - [x] unit/integration tests for cache lifecycle - [x] docs and runbook updated - [x] Linear tickets linked Related Linear: ENG-3129 (presubmit perf), ENG-3180 (release automation signal). CI: initial run showed a flaky python-lint failure on windows runners (flake in dependency resolver) — fixed by pinning pip-tools extraction in the runner image within the second commit. Impact: average presubmit latency reduced 55% for small PRs in early opt-in telemetry; overall CI CPU cost increased slightly (~6%) due to scorer compute but net developer time saved is positive. How to verify locally: see doc/dev/ci-presubmit-quickstart.md. Merge: squash and merge after approvals.

review_comments: Rohit Malhotra: Can the cache key handle renames? Suggest including directory-level mtime fallback — Ava: added rename handling by normalizing git index path and falling back to aggregate mtime in hash util (see hash.go).

Sofia Martinez: scorer looks useful but could produce false positives on large autogenerated protobuf diffs — Ava: added a file-type weight table and excluded generated/ by default in scorer config, plus an env override to include for teams who want it.

Liam O'Connor: we should gate scorer runtime to keep the fastpath <2m — Ava: scorer now runs with a 30s timeout in the staged job and writes partial output if timed out; fallback to 'unknown' score so release automation degrades gracefully.

release_notes: Reduced presubmit latency for small PRs via per-package lint cache and added a machine-readable release sanity score. Opt-in rollout behind CI_LINT_FASTPATH. See doc/dev/ci-presubmit-quickstart.md for verification steps.
